title: Malicious code in sitecard (PyPI)
description: The PyPI package 'sitecard' versions 0.1.0 through 0.1.14 contains malicious code that creates an SSH session exposed via tunnels. This session is accessible without any authentication by default and reports to a hardcoded location, effectively acting as a backdoor. This exposes users to unauthorized remote access by attackers.
aiSummary: The 'sitecard' package on PyPI provides functionality to create SSH sessions exposed through tunnels. However, the package contains malicious code that by default allows the created SSH session to be accessed without any authentication. Additionally, the session details are reported to a hardcoded remote location, enabling attackers to gain unauthorized access to affected systems. This behavior classifies the package as a backdoor with clear malicious intent.
aiImpact: Users installing or using affected versions of the 'sitecard' package risk unauthorized remote access to their systems due to the unauthenticated SSH session. This can lead to compromise of system confidentiality, integrity, and availability. The hardcoded reporting mechanism further facilitates attacker control and monitoring of compromised systems.
